Visit note | 2025-11-13 04:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Habiba Akand, 47, female. Mrs. Akand returns for review, explaining that she experiences a throbbing headache on one side of her head, accompanied by nausea and her eyes hurting in bright light. She mentions that these attacks are often triggered by skipping meals while travelling in Gazipur. She works as a tailor and notes having about 8 headache days a month. She has no other significant medical conditions and denies any visual blurring or weakness. On examination: BP 116/84 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 57 kg. Cranial nerves are intact and neurological exam is normal. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up in 3 months with the headache diary.

Visit note | 2025-11-13 04:00 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Rakib Hossain, 43, male. Mr. Hossain attends for his first visit complaining of sudden breathlessness during attacks, an intense fear of dying, and notes that his previous heart tests were completely normal. He reports that his very first attack happened while he was trapped in a crowded lift in Shyamoli. He works as a rickshaw puller and reports experiencing about 8 panic attacks in the last month. He has no chronic medical illnesses and denies any chest pain or chronic cough. On examination: BP 114/76 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 44 kg. He appears anxious but is cooperative and oriented. Assessment: Panic disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to practise slow breathing during attacks, reduce caffeine intake, and start regular counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-11-13 04:30 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Saad Uddin, 39, male. Mr. Uddin attends for review, reporting that he gets breathless when walking up stairs and has noticed he looks pale. He believes this worsened after a long spell of poor meals while living alone in Khilgaon. He works as a cricket coach. His presentation includes a craving to chew ice and a sore smooth tongue along with tiredness. Laboratory results show haemoglobin 10.0 g/dL. He has no comorbid conditions. On examination: BP 126/70 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, weight 93 kg. Conjunctivae are pale, and cardiovascular and respiratory examinations are otherwise unremarkable. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and to avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin test.

Visit note | 2025-11-13 04:30 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Bushra Akter, 80, female. Mrs. Akter comes in for a follow-up visit, stating she feels a heavy feeling in her chest that eases with rest within minutes, along with chest tightness when walking fast or climbing. She first noticed this while climbing to a fourth-floor flat in Savar. She works as a farmer. She has no known comorbidities and denies any night-time shortness of breath or palpitations. On examination: BP 150/85 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 62 kg. Heart sounds are normal with no added murmurs. Assessment: Stable angina. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid heavy exertion until review, walk 20 minutes daily on flat ground, and stop smoking. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and fasting lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-11-13 04:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Shathi Sikder, 72, female. Mrs. Sikder comes for a review visit, reporting a sour taste in her mouth, symptoms that are worse when lying down, and a burning sensation behind her breastbone after meals. She was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up in 1 month.
